normalized_notes: supp3 index p.1 names efigure 1a 'residual ... (expected - observed)'; caption on p.24 (rendered) says left/negative = mace lower than mean, right/positive = higher. under e-o, positive residual means lower than expected. sign conventions conflict.

main p.4: 'the lower limit of the confidence interval was greater than the threshold of noninferiority, thus noninferiority was not demonstrated'; the lower limit -1.64% is below the -1% margin. recomputed 44/1018 vs 43/1022: rd 0.11, wald 95% lower bound -1.64, p(ni) 0.106. wording reversed; conclusion correct.

table 2 p.6 pp rows. survival 28 d 54/995 vs 51/943: wald rd 0.02 (-2.00 to 2.04), newcombe -2.03 to 2.05; printed 0.1 (-10 to 9.7). admission 289/995 vs 312/943: -4.04 (-8.16 to 0.08); printed -4.0 (-7.6 to 0.6). itt rows reproduce exactly.

table 2 p.6 pp rosc eti '377 (30.0)': 377/943 = 39.98%, so 40.0% expected. printed difference -5.6 matches 34.4 - 40.0 (computed -5.61) and p .01 matches chi-square 0.011. percentage typo; printed 30.0 would reverse direction.

supp2 etable 2 p.3: ecmo/donation-excluded row 43/971 vs 39/978, printed 0.4 [-2.2, 1.3]. wald gives 0.44 (-1.34 to 2.22), newcombe -1.37 to 2.26; printed limits look mirrored. companion row 41/863 vs 45/1174 reproduces (0.92, -0.88 to 2.71 vs 0.9 [-0.9, 2.7]).

table 2 p.6 (and abstract) rrs do not equal low/intermediate risk ratios: ards 17/448 vs 23/462 gives rr 0.76 (0.41-1.41), printed 0.86 (0.59-1.24); extrapulmonary infection 0.74 (0.42-1.29) vs 0.84 (0.60-1.18). all 10 printed rrs and cis reproduce as p(low arm | event)/p(low arm | no event), i.e., a transposed 2x2 table. p values (chi-square) are correct.
supp3 etable 2 p.6 (rendered): other mode, after titration, intermediate-arm peep '8 (5 - 1)'. a third quartile of 1 cannot lie below a median of 8; likely a truncated value (e.g., 10).

methods p.4: imv cumulative incidence compared with the gray test; supp2 efigure 1 p.3 (rendered) labels the same comparison 'p (log rank test) = 0.17'; table 2 prints p = .17 beside the cause-specific hr.

table 1 p.4 (n = 388 per arm): hfno liver 45 (13.3), control kidney 69 (20.4), postextubation 14 (4.1) and 18 (5.3). with 388: 11.6%, 17.8%, 3.6%, 4.6%; all four printed values equal count/338. other cells reproduce with 388.

figure 3 p.7 (rendered) all-patient hrs are reciprocals of table 2: mortality 1.02 (0.81-1.29) vs 0.98 (0.77-1.24); imv 1.17 (0.94-1.46) vs 0.85 (0.68-1.06). so forest hrs are standard vs hfno, yet hr < 1 is labelled 'favors high-flow'. e.g., imv non-hematologic 61/199 (30.7%) vs 89/198 (44.9%) plotted as hr 1.61 on the 'favors standard' side.

table 2 p.5 icu-acquired infection 39/388 vs 41/388, cause-specific hr 1.01 (0.96 to 1.06). with 80 events se(log hr) is about sqrt(1/39+1/41) = 0.224, giving roughly 0.65-1.57; printed interval implies se 0.025. same construction reproduces the mortality and imv rows.

main p.6: 'vasopressors and renal replacement therapy were needed in 153 patients (19.7%) randomized to high-flow ... and 31 patients (4%) randomized to standard oxygen ... with no statistical difference'. 153/776 = 19.7% and 31/776 = 4.0%: pooled percentages, apparently vasopressors and rrt overall, misattributed to arms.
abstract p.1 prints 'risk difference, 0.4% [95% ci, -9.4% to 8.7%]'; main p.5 and table 2 p.7 print -0.4. recomputed 117/240 - 111/226 = -0.37 points (wald -9.4 to 8.7). abstract sign dropped.

methods p.4: cox model censored at 6 months; supp2 efigure 2 p.5 (rendered) runs to 250 days with 91/88 at risk at 200 days and 23/17 at 250 days. display contradicts the stated 6-month window; curves are flat after about 100 days.

table 2 p.7: rr, ci and p for the two bleeding rows are swapped. intracranial 47/260 vs 37/240: rr 1.17 (0.79-1.74), p 0.43 (printed 1.23 (0.43-3.5), .70); extracranial 8/260 vs 6/240: rr 1.23 (0.43-3.50), p 0.70 (printed 1.17 (0.79-1.74), .43). rds correct; supp2 etable 6 p values are correct.

supp1 p.192 (dsmc report, 17 july 2016; rendered): favorable-outcome table for group y sums cumulatively to 7, 9, 20, ... 73, but the cumulative y line plots about 6, 12, 17, 22, ... 80, which equals cumulative unfavorable counts (13-7, 8-2, 16-11, ...). x line matches favorable sums.
supp2 etable 10 p.18 (as-treated baseline), normothermia (n = 196): marshall v printed '34.7 (68)' and vi '1 (2)'. 68/196 = 34.7%, so count and percent are transposed; 1/196 = 0.5%, not 2.
supp2 p.22 (rendered): adjusted or printed '0.95 (0.55-275 1.64) p = .84'. the '275' is a stray token; intended interval is evidently 0.55-1.64.

abstract p.1: '22% men'. main p.4: 22 men and 8 women enrolled (22/30 = 73.3%); table 1 p.5: 13 + 7 = 20 men among 27 completers (74%). abstract percentage is wrong (apparently the count printed as a percent).

main p.4: in 3 patients 'bayesian analysis showed the predefined clinical ineffectiveness'. supp2 etable 3 p.5 (rendered): patients 13 and 22 have posterior probabilities 2% and 1% (<20%), but patient 11 has 38%; its footnote explains a judgment-based stop. only 2 met the rule.

table 1 p.5 (rendered): inqol composite median (iqr) 84.0 (74.5-110.3) clcn1 and 98.0 (56.0-120.0) scn4a; footnote f gives a 0-100 scale (also table 2 fn g, methods p.3). upper quartiles exceed the scale maximum.

table 2 p.7 scn4a fifth-attempt transient paresis: effect 13.71 (-1.96 to 25.47), p = .02. the ci includes 0 (ci-implied p about .05) and is asymmetric about 13.71; period changes -5.00 (placebo) and +9.56 (mexiletine) mean mexiletine worsened paresis, contradicting fn d ('all significant findings favored mexiletine'). repeated in text p.6.

table 2 p.7 lower header: 'treatment effect (placebo-mexiletine)'. lower-section effects equal mexiletine minus placebo changes: inqol -21.44 - (-7.22) = -14.22 (printed -14.22); eyelid first -4.99 - (-0.74) = -4.25; tug first -1.41 - (-0.15) = -1.26 (printed -1.25). upper ivr section uses placebo minus mexiletine (5.55 - 2.42 = 3.13).
table 2 p.7 mental sf-36 effect 6.78 (1.64 to 11.92), p = .001. the interval implies t-test p = 0.012 (df 26) or z p = 0.010. printed p is about 10 times too small; significance at .05 unchanged.

table 2 p.7 first-attempt handgrip, placebo change 0.46 (-0.30 to -1.23) (minus sign visible in render): the upper limit is below the lower limit and the mean lies outside; likely 1.23. treatment effect row reproduces (-2.39 - 0.46 = -2.85).

table 2 p.7 scn4a fifth-attempt handgrip: -1.96 (-3.41 to 0.51), p = .009 (repeated p.8 text). ci includes 0 (ci-implied p about .05) and is asymmetric about -1.96 (midpoint -1.45). period changes give mexiletine - placebo = -1.95, so the estimate fits the period data but not the interval or p.
table 2 p.7 timed up&go mean, placebo change 0.07 (-0.67 to 0.01): estimate above the upper limit; symmetric limit would be about 0.81. treatment effect -1.12 = -1.05 - 0.07 reproduces.
table 2 p.8 needle emg grading: 0.67 (0.23 to 1.11), p < .001. interval implies p = 0.004 (t, df 26) or 0.003 (z). printed p too small; significance unchanged.

table 1 p.5 (rendered): saturation <90% and <80% use denominators 352 and 344, but footnote b says 19 and 24 patients lacked saturation (implying 362 and 352). 352 and 344 equal arm totals minus the patients missing heart rate (29 and 32).

table 1 p.5 nested medical indications: altered mental status, cardiac arrest, septic shock and seizure percentages use the arm total (185/381 = 48.6%; 173/376 = 46.0%), while asthma/copd and 'other' use the medical subtotal (16/318 = 5.0%, 44/318 = 13.8%; 23/315 = 7.3%, 41/315 = 13.0%). denominator not stated.
table 3 p.7 (rendered) all-patient first-attempt duration: difference '1 (4 to -1)'; limits transposed. supp2 etable 1 p.2 (clustered analysis) prints 1 s (-1 s to 4 s).

text p.4: 'a total of 4800 patients were enrolled ... and included in the primary analysis'; table 2 uses 2400 per arm (all-or-none 1290/2400, 1147/2400). figure 1 p.5 (rendered) labels 2003 and 1977 (12-month completers) as 'patients included in primary analysis'.

table 3 p.8 in-hospital death 11/2400 vs 23/2400: adjusted difference -0.7 (-1.1 to 0.2), p .009. interval includes 0 and implies p about .035; it is also asymmetric about -0.7. the adjacent hr 0.96 (0.90-1.02) is implausibly precise for 34 deaths (crude ratio 0.48; se(log) about 0.37).

supp2 etable 1 p.2: 3-month adjusted bmi difference -0.01 (-0.12, 0.13), p 0.83. interval midpoint is +0.005; other rows are centred on their estimates (e.g., -0.04 (-0.20, 0.12)). with +0.01 (unrounded about 0.014) the p of 0.83 also fits. sign error likely.

figure 1 (main p. 3, rendered) labels 1451 online exclusions 'bmi <15 or >40', while eappendix 1 (supp3 p. 3) states the online tool used bmi 25-40, as do the abstract and methods. the lower cutoff of 15 contradicts 25; the later 18 telephone exclusions for bmi <25 leave open which cutoff was applied online.

main p. 4: '392 participants (196 in each of the 4 possible intervention combinations)'; 4 x 196 = 784, not 392. power.prop.test(p1=.20, p2=.30, power=.90) gives n = 391.9 per group, so 392 is the size of each main-effect arm (2 cells x 196), not the total. 196/0.78 = 251.3, consistent with 250 per cell.

eappendix 10 table b (supp3 p. 19, rendered): spain 0.107 (-0.424 to 0.520), uk 0.117 (-0.371 to 0.638), germany 0.058 (-0.401 to 0.606) are not centered (midpoints 0.048, 0.134, 0.102) while all six other rows are. 2b-l gives 0.638, 0.605, 0.517: the upper limits appear rotated among the three site rows.

main p. 6/table 2: missed doses 4.6% (sd 1.0) vs 4.3% (sd 0.5), welch t test p = .87. welch with n = 96/98: t = 2.63, df = 139, p = .009 (n = 107/109: p = .006). p = .87 would need sds of about 12.5 points. summary statistics and p value are incompatible; one is misreported. the 0.3-point difference is clinically trivial either way.

etable 9 (supp1 p. 15, rendered): serious systemic diarrhea, mycophenolate column (n = 20) shows 1 (3.4). 1/20 = 5.0%; 1/29 = 3.4% (the methotrexate column n). other entries in the same column use n = 20 (e.g., allergic reaction 1 (5.0)). percentage computed with wrong denominator.

main table 3 (p. 7, rendered 200 dpi): alcohol 12-mo difference -0.2 (95% ci -0.4 to 0.1), p = .01; etables 5 and 8 give the 12-mo ci as -0.4 to -0.1 and -0.3 to -0.1, so the main-table '0.1' has likely lost its minus sign. the 6-mo rows with an upper limit of 0 and p = .01/.02 can be reproduced by rounding (e.g., -0.18, -0.33 to -0.03 gives p = .02).

etable 2 (supp3 p. 7, rendered): intervention baseline red wine median (iqr) 33 (0, 29) g/week. a median cannot exceed the upper quartile (33 > 29). control prints 4 (0, 29), so 33 is probably a typographic error (e.g., 3).

efigure 2 (supp3 p. 26, rendered): printed percentages inside the bars contradict bar heights: e.g., mufa:sfa bars about 87% (intervention) and 79% (control) but labels 79% and 86%; fruit about 63/58 vs labels 58/63; vegetables about 65/56 vs 56/64; dessert about 68/60 vs 59/58. labels look swapped between arms for most pairs, and dessert fits no swap.

etable 2 (supp2 p. 4, rendered): hypercapnic cells 14/45 (69), 16/59 (73), 20/46 (57), 23/61 (62). correct percentages are 31.1, 27.1, 43.5, 37.7; each printed value equals 100 minus the correct one (68.9, 72.9, 56.5, 62.3). counts are correct: they sum with the nonhypercapnic cells to table 1 totals (65/284, 86/322, 121/288, 114/326).

figure 3 (main p. 8, rendered) lists 703 under placebo and 609 under vitamin d, but vitamin d arms total 370+333 = 703 and placebo 289+320 = 609; figure 4 lists 659 placebo / 653 omega-3, whereas omega-3 = 370+289 = 659. stratum rows confirm the swap (e.g., omega-3-placebo stratum: 333 under placebo = vitamin d+placebo arm). efigures 2-3 repeat it. mean changes sit in the correct columns.

figure 2 (main p. 7, rendered): panels b and d (omega-3 vs placebo) repeat the vitamin d panel counts (placebo 607/459/438 and active 701/531/496 for egfr; 609/463/440 and 702/529/505 for acr). table 2 gives omega-3 egfr counts 657/499/472 (active) and 651/491/462 (placebo).

etable 2 (supp2 p. 7, rendered) year 5: every other row in the vitamin d columns implies nonmissing n of 489-494 (active) and 422-425 (placebo), e.g., biguanides 325 (66), 313 (74). sglt2 25 (6) and 21 (4) then give 5.1% and 5.0%, both printed wrongly; fish-oil columns reconcile. overall 46/916 = 5.0%.

etable 7 (supp2 p. 12): title n = 944 and arm counts 504+440 = 477+467 = 944, but the footnote says 1311 donated baseline urine and '991 of these also donated a year 5 urine sample and were included', with 320 excluded (1311-320 = 991). 1311-944 = 367. main text p. 4 gives 945 year-5 urine donors, consistent with 944 plus 1 without baseline.

efigures 2-3 (supp2 pp. 18-19, rendered) plot the ratio of acr change, active/placebo; a ratio >1 means a larger albuminuria increase with the active supplement, i.e., favors placebo. the axis labels put 'favors vitamin d' / 'favors omega-3' on the right (>1) and 'favors placebo' on the left. direction labels are reversed. all intervals cross 1.

table 2 footnote a (main p. 7): 'hr values greater than 1 indicate that vitamin d supplementation was associated with a decreased probability of the outcome.' the text interprets hr <1 as benefit (e.g., relapse shr 0.44 in the middle subgroup 'significantly lower in the vitamin d group', p. 6; hr 0.76 for relapse or death). the footnote reverses the direction used everywhere else.

primary composite 211/989 vs 233/987: abstract, table 3 (p. 9) and figure 2 give 'risk ratio 0.93 (0.83-1.04)'; efigure 12 (supp4 p. 42, rendered) lists the identical tuple as 'odds ratio (95% ci)' for the collapsed composite. crude rr = 0.90 (0.77-1.06) and crude or = 0.88, so 0.93 matches neither label.

abstract (p. 1): hypoxemia 5.0% vs 13.6%, 'difference, -8.6% [95% ci, -11.1% to 6.1%]; p < .001'. table 3 (p. 9): -8.6 (-11.1 to -6.1). recomputed wald ci for 49/989 vs 134/987: -11.2 to -6.1. the abstract upper limit has lost its minus sign.

the 'risk ratio' column (table 3, figure 2, etable 8, efigure 12) does not equal the ratio of group risks. for most rows it equals the high-peep risk divided by the pooled risk: pleural effusion 43/989 vs 21/987 crude rr 2.04, printed 1.35 (pooled-ratio 1.34); mortality 12 vs 5 crude 2.40, printed 1.41 (1.41); dic 1 vs 0 printed 2.00 (2.00); ards 3 vs 1 crude 2.99, printed 1.50 (1.50).

table 2 (p. 8, rendered): monitoring 632/982 (64.9) and 651/984 (67.7); reversal 724/982 (74.3) and 723/984 (75.2). 632/982 = 64.4%, 651/984 = 66.2%, 724/982 = 73.7%, 723/984 = 73.5%. the printed percentages equal counts over the neuromuscular-blockade denominators 974/961 (64.9, 67.7, 74.3, 75.2), whereas the differences (-1.8, 0.2) use 982/984.

table 3 (p. 9): disseminated intravascular coagulation 1 (0.1) vs 0, 'rr 2.00 (1.91 to 2.09)', p > .99. a ci excluding 1 is incompatible with p > .99 (fisher p = 1.0), and a finite rr with a narrow ci is not estimable from 1 vs 0 events. 2.00 equals the high-peep risk over the pooled risk (see c004).

table 3 (p. 9): in-hospital mortality 12 (1.2) vs 5 (0.5), rr 1.41 (0.95 to 1.81), p = .09. on the log scale the interval is asymmetric (0.395 below vs 0.250 above the estimate) unlike neighboring rows, and it is far too narrow for 17 deaths: crude rr 2.40 (0.85-6.77). the p value matches an uncorrected chi-square test on the counts (.089); the estimate and interval do not.

etable 8 per-protocol (supp4 p. 29, rendered): cardiopulmonary edema 15/917 vs 7/912, 'effect estimate 1.36 (1.02-1.82)', p = 0.09. the interval excludes 1 while p > .05. crude rr = 2.13 (0.87-5.20), uncorrected chi-square p = .089, matching the printed p; 1.36 equals the high-peep/pooled risk ratio (c004).

main p1 abstract and p3 results print the surgery hba1c change as 1.6% with 95% ci -1.8% to -1.3% (point outside its interval) and the medical change as 0.2% (-0.5% to 0.2%); table 2 p6 gives signed -1.6 and -0.2 with the same cis. mixed sign convention; direction is clear from 'decreased' and table 2.

year-12 hba1c difference -1.1% (-1.7 to -0.5) is given p=.002 in main p1/p3 but p<.001 in etable 2 (supp 2 p15), same model and interval. wald p from the ci = .0003 (worst-case rounding .0015); the two printed p values conflict; inference unchanged.

abstract p1: '4 deaths (2.2%), 2 in each group' with n=262 enrolled; 4/262 = 1.5%. table 3 p8 arm values 2/96=2.1% and 2/166=1.2% reproduce. no alternative denominator is stated. counts are correct, so the percentage alone is wrong.

etable 1 (supp 2 p14), 7-year column n=262: other race 4 (1.9); 4/262=1.5%. race counts 81+176+4=261, not 262; main table 1 gives white 59+118=177 (67.6%) and other 2+2=4, whereas etable 1 and the abstract give white 176 (67.2%).

main p4: follow-up imaging was mri in 8 of 336 (2%) and ct in 328 (98%); p9 and etable 11 (supp 5 p51; n 101+24+79=204) describe 204 (61%) patients with mr diffusion follow-up; p11 says 'two-thirds'. the count of the post hoc infarct-growth population is irreconcilable within the report.

efigures 7 and 8 (supp 5 p13-14): aspects 0-2 (n=19) has 0 events in both arms for mrs 0-2 and for mrs 0-3, yet both print rr 1.00 (0.37-2.72), identical across outcomes; other zero-cell rows (e.g., >=150 ml) print '*'. a risk ratio is not estimable with no events in either arm.

figure 2b (main p7, core >=100 ml): segment colors assign evt 2/6/10/20 to mrs 0-3 (no mrs 4 segment), giving mrs 0-2 18% and 0-3 38%; efigures 7-8 give 4/51 (7.8%) and 9/51 (17.6%), and the discussion says about 80% had mrs >=4. the values fit if each segment is shifted one category (mrs 1-6); mm bar shows the same shift.

main p8 states that as mismatch volume increased the marginal probability of mrs 0-2 and 0-3 increased with evt and decreased with mm; efigure 17a/b (supp 5 p23) shows both evt curves (and mm curves) decreasing across mismatch volume.

efigure 13 (supp 5 p19), rr of mrs 5-6 (adverse) with evt vs mm: all 16 rrs are below 1 (favoring evt), but the axis labels read 'favours medical management' on the left and 'favours thrombectomy' on the right. efigure 9 (p15), the same outcome, labels the axis correctly.

discordant profile 2 (aspects 6-10, core >=70 ml): etable 9 mm has mrs 0-3 3/11 and mrs 5-6 10/11 (13 > 11); etable 10 mm has 4/12 and 11/12 (15 > 12) and mrs 0-2 2/12 with 11/12. etable 8 attributes the favorable counts to evt (mrs 0-2 1/12, 0-3 3/12; mm 0/11), so arms appear swapped for favorable outcomes in etables 9-10.

main p2 says the waitlist group was not included in tests of statistical significance; p4 reports retention p=.02 (1 month) and p=.11 (7 months). these reproduce only as 3-group chi-square tests including waitlist (p=.017, .115); the 2-group tests give p=.009 and .073. conclusions about retention are unchanged.

etable 5 (supp 2 p14), 30-day iprw or 1.92 (1.50, 2.24): a log-symmetric interval with lower 1.50 implies an upper limit near 2.46 (1.92^2/1.50); all 11 other rr/or cells in the table are log-symmetric within rounding. the iprw interval is also narrower than the cca or interval, unlike the rr rows.

table s7 (supp 1 p20) headers say n=233/238 (per-protocol) but its site totals 256+245=501 and events 4+7=11, 19+15=34 are the primary analysis population; table s8 (p21), titled per-protocol, has headers n=249/252 although its counts reproduce with 233/238 (9/233=3.9%, 33/238=13.9%, 20/238=8.4%). the two tables' headers appear swapped.

table s6 (supp 1 p19), center-adjusted primary analysis with n=249/252, gives balloon events 9 (3.9) vs 11 (4.4) in table 2 and figure 2; 9/249=3.6%, whereas 9/233=3.9% matches the per-protocol count (table s8). adjustment does not change event counts; the hr 0.32 (0.16-0.62) matches the main analysis, suggesting a transcription error in the count.

table 2 (main p8), any stroke outside the qualifying territory within 1 year, 3 (1.2) vs 4 (1.6): incidence difference -0.4 (95% ci -2.4 to -1.7), hr 0.76, p=.72. the point lies outside its interval and the interval excludes 0. wald recomputation gives -0.38 (-2.44 to 1.67): the upper limit has lost its sign.
figure s4 (supp 1 p13), balloon group mrs 2 at 90 days: '2.0 (n=50)'; 50/249=20.1%, and with 50 the category counts sum to 294, not 249. n=5 gives 2.0% and a total of 249 (205+36+5+2+0+1+0).

etable 10 (supp 2 p13-14), mouth sores among sspedi>=3: symptom screening 0/0 (empty), yet finite ors are printed: 2.6 (0.04-170.4), 5.00 (0.07-366.4) twice. these equal haldane 0.5-corrected crude ors ((0.5x6.5)/(0.5x2.5)=2.6; (0.5x7.5)/(0.5x1.5)=5.0), a method not described; a comparison with an empty group is not estimable.

etable 10 symptom-specific intervention, sspedi>=1: neuropathy 6/57 vs 0/70, or 17.8 (0.98-323.1), p=.007; hunger 6/111 vs 0/130, or 16.08 (0.9-288.74), p=.009; main p6 calls both significant. recomputed: the ors/cis are haldane-corrected wald values and the p values are fisher exact (.0070, .0089), not the logistic models the footnote states. ci and p come from different, undisclosed methods.

abstract (main p1): 'among the 338 randomized infants ..., 320 underwent operative repair'. figure 1 (p3) and text (p4-5) give 152 early (147+5) and 129 late (90+39) repairs = 281; 320 is the number remaining after withdrawals (163+157), the population described in table 1.

abstract (p1) and results (p5) state no significant difference in any of the 11 secondary end points, but table 2 (p6) gives eq-5d-5l postoperative day 5 difference -0.057 (95% ci -0.111 to -0.003), p=.04, favoring placebo. the sap (p14) specifies no multiplicity adjustment and time-point effects from the time-by-treatment model.

subgroup efigure (supp 3 p2): legend labels the horizontal lines '99% ci', while the caption says the numbers are 95% cis. the plotted lines coincide with the printed numeric limits (e.g., overall 0.88-1.07; low eras 0.49-2.08), and the overall row equals the main 95% ci. sap p15 specifies 99% cis for subgroups.

abstract (p1): patients were 'randomly assigned ... restrictive (n = 733) or liberal (n = 724)' and '1979 randomized, 1508 completed the trial'. figure 1 (p3): 983 restrictive and 994 liberal randomized (plus 2 lost envelopes = 1979); 750/758 remained after post-randomization exclusions; 17 and 34 then withdrew or were lost, leaving 733/724 analyzed. the n's labeled as randomized are analyzed counts, and 1508 did not all complete the trial.

liberal group, ais <3 subgroup: figure 4 (main p8) prints 48/473 (10.1%), etable 7 (supp 2 p20) 48/473 (9.2%). 48/473 = 10.1%, but 473 + 202 (ais >=3) = 675, not 724; 48/522 = 9.2% and 522 + 202 = 724. the denominator 473 is probably wrong in both displays (restrictive 500 + 233 = 733 reconciles).

etable 1 (supp 2 p14), receiving center bern: 50/750 (7.2) and 47/758 (6.7); 50/750 = 6.7% and 47/758 = 6.2%. other receiving-center percentages are also slightly off (335/750 = 44.7 printed 44.4; 348/758 = 45.9 printed 45.7), though the counts sum to 750 and 758.
etable 2 (supp 2 p15), transport walk-in, liberal: 4/743 (5.3); 4/743 = 0.54%. typographic error (decimal place); the category totals (585+141+9+3+4+1 = 743) confirm the count.

etable 2 (supp 2 p15), surgery in the trauma resuscitation room, vascular surgery, liberal: 0/747 (1.1). a zero numerator cannot give 1.1%; either the count or the percentage is wrong. also in the same table, restrictive firearm injury has denominator 724 (8/724) where all other mechanism rows use 742.

etable 10 (supp 2 p24) prints 55/750 (45), 67/758 (55), 174/750 (51), 165/758 (49); the percentages are shares of excluded patients (55/122, 67/122, 174/339, 165/339), not of 750/758, and post-randomization exclusions are not part of the 750/758. also 55 + 67 = 122 vs n = 130 stated (figure 1: 59 and 71); the difference equals the 4 + 4 'omitted according to swiss law', which the footnote does not mention.

abstract (p1): cnrt 90 (47%) continued, 50 (33%) increased, 51 (34%) switched; 90/191=47% but 50/151=33% and 51/151=34% (sum 114%). varenicline: 39 (32%) and 41 (34%) of 122, but 77 (49%) of 157. mixed denominators within the same sentence.

cnrt nonabstainers, switch to varenicline (or increase) vs continuation: abstract (p1) rd 6% (95% cri 6% to 11%); results (p5) 6% (2%-11%); etable 4 (supp 2 p21) 6% (2%-10%) for switch and 6% (2%-11%) for increase. the abstract lower limit is wrong.

varenicline nonabstainers: switch to cnrt 0/41 (0%) vs continue 2/77 (3%). results (p5) give rd -3% (-4% to -1%) with '>99% probability that continuing was worse than switching' (direction reversed); etable 4 prints +3% (1% to 4%) for switch vs stay; the abstract attributes the >99% statement to 'switching to a higher dosage'. discussion (p8) correctly describes a decrement with switching.

eot+30 continuous abstinence, varenicline nonabstainers who continued: main p7 and supp 2 p10 give n = 42; efigure 2 (supp 2 p15) gives 0/77, the continuation group used in all analyses (42 re-randomized + 35 assigned).

main p7 (and supp 2 p10): at 6 months 'only the cnrt patch increase (3%) and varenicline dosage increase (2%) provided benefit over continuation (0%)'. efigure 3 (supp 2 p16) and supp p11: cnrt+ 6% (3/50) vs cnrt continuation 3% (3/90); rd 3% (etable 9). the cnrt figures conflate an rd with an arm rate and misstate continuation as 0%.

supp 2 p8: revised intercept prior 'normal(mean = 0, variance = 10)', with odds 95% interval 3.07e-9 to 325,215,956. that interval corresponds to sd = 10 (variance 100); variance 10 (sd 3.16) gives 0.0020 to 492. the main text (p4) also writes the coefficient prior as n(mu=0, sigma=1000), i.e., sd notation.

six-month continuous abstinence, phase 1 abstainers (cnrt 39% vs varenicline 40%): supp 2 p12 gives ard 1.0% (-1.3% to 1.1%), probability 55%; etable 11 (p35) gives 1% (-11% to 12%), 56%. the narrative interval is wrong (scale error), and the sign is ambiguous (cnrt minus varenicline would be about -1%).

primary between-group difference in vas change: abstract (p1), results (p7), table 2 (p6) and etable 1 (supp 3 p2) give -0.3 (-0.27), consistent with placebo minus krill (-20.2 - (-19.9)); key points (p2) gives +0.30 with the same ci (-6.9 to 6.4). the direction convention is not defined anywhere.
placebo composition: methods (p2-3) 'less than 5 mg/g (0.5%)' of other omega-3; discussion (p9) 'less than 5 mg/g (0.05%)'. 5 mg/g = 0.5%; the discussion value is off by a factor of 10.

methods (p4): icoap item scores 0-4 (never to very often); constant 0-20, intermittent 0-24, total 0-44. table 1 footnote g (p5): 5 constant and 8 intermittent questions with responses 'not at all' to 'extremely'. 8 x 4 = 32, not 24 (icoap has 6 intermittent items), and total would be 52.

under the placebo-minus-krill convention that reproduces other rows (e.g., vas -20.2-(-19.9)=-0.3; icoap intermittent 1.5; function week 4 -19): icoap total (table 2) -8.2-(-9.9)=1.7 vs printed 2.05; womac weight-bearing week 4 (supp 3 p5) -103-(-84)=-19 vs printed 3 (the arm changes duplicate the function row); hscrp week 12 (p6) 0.24-(-0.53)=0.77 vs printed 0.07.

table 3 (p8) vs etable 7 (supp 3 p10-11): cough krill 2/placebo 0 vs 0/2; nasopharyngitis 2/1 vs 1/2; gerd 1/3 vs 3/1; abdominal discomfort 0/3 vs 3/0; diarrhea 2/1 vs 1/2; pain in extremity 1/6 vs 1/5 (abstract 1/5). etable 7 subrows sum to the class totals (respiratory 9/16; gi 13/6), so table 3 subrows are attributed to the wrong arm.

table 3 (p8): 'any treatment-related serious adverse event' 0 and 0; footnote b and text: no saes related to treatment / all unrelated. etable 8 (supp 3 p14) rates relationship as possible for most saes and probable for one krill oil sae (transfusion-dependent anaemia), unlikely for two.

etable 4 (supp 3 p6): fasting glucose week-12 contrast 0.07 (-1.19 to 1.33) has exactly the interval of the hscrp week-12 row; with arm cis about 0.3 wide, a 2.5-wide contrast interval cannot be right. the womac total week-24 interval being narrower than a root-sum-of-squares of arm intervals is not by itself an error, since arm changes share model coefficients.

etable 5 (supp 3 p8), worms effusion change: percentages are identical in both arms and match pooled proportions (e.g., smaller by 1 unit 26/216 = 12.0%; no change 155/216 = 72%), not arm-specific ones (10/107 = 9.3%; 16/109 = 14.7%; 80/107 = 74.8%; 75/109 = 68.8%).

main p.1 abstract counts quality of life among secondary outcomes with no significant difference and p.6 says no qol differences citing etables 2-4, but supp3 etable 3 p.4 shows day-7 eq-5d index md -0.057 (-0.104 to -0.010), p=.02 (ci-implied p=.017), a sap-planned day-specific contrast with no multiplicity correction (sap p.26, p.12). summary claim contradicts the cited table.

main p.3 and supp3 p.10 list cox covariates as prebaseline slope, months since onset, riluzole, edaravone and age; table 2 footnote b (main p.7) lists the same plus sex. same models, two covariate sets; which was fitted is not determinable.

main p.4 gives model mortality rates 0.007 (shared placebo) and 0.006 (cnm-au8) events/month citing etable 2; etable 2 (supp3 p.15) gives 0.010 and 0.009 (median and mean). slope cris also differ (main -1.176 to -0.892 and -1.153 to -0.858 vs etable -1.181 to -0.894 and -1.143 to -0.847).

main p.4 says '4 of the 41 participants in the regimen placebo group and 2 in the shared placebo group were excluded' for no follow-up time, but table 2 (p.7) uses 4/41 as regimen-placebo events and only 2 shared-placebo exclusions (164-2=162). the sentence misattributes the 4 events as exclusions.

etable 3b serum nfl rows (supp3 p.17) are on the natural-log x100 scale although labeled % change: placebo 26.8 = 100*log-change (exp(0.268)-1=30.7%, main p.8 says 30.8%), contrast -26.4 (-50.3,-2.6) back-transforms to -23.2% (-39.5%,-2.6%) = main p.8. plasma rows are back-transformed. 60-mg serum ci (-45.1,-0.7) is also asymmetric about -27.4.

main p.4: paintrainer '371 (43%) completed at least 6 sessions'; figure 1 (p.5) gives 776 randomized, 371/156/249 completing 6-8/1-5/0 sessions. 371/776 = 47.8% (printed 43%). neighbors reproduce: 527/776 = 67.9% (68%), 548/778 = 70.4% (70%), 660/778 = 84.8% (85%).

main p.4 and table 3 footnote d define smd = adjusted md / sd of change in usual care at that time, so within a row the three smds share one sd. for 19 of 21 rows (pp.10-11) no single sd reproduces all three smds from the printed mds within rounding; 4 smds have the opposite sign to their md (eg physical 3 mo hc vs uc md 0.7, smd -0.02). text p.7 also cites 3-month smds -0.26/-0.36, which are the 6-month values.

table 2 (main p.9) hc vs pt: six cells whose rr ci includes 1 print finite positive nnt intervals, eg 24 (12-186) beside rr 1.13 (0.98-1.30). these six cells, and only these, use an en dash, and etables 7-8 (supp4 pp.11, 14) print the same construction with a signed nnh limit, eg 31 (13, -60). upper limits are nnh values with the minus sign lost; implied nnh from rr limits 152, 70, 59, 39, 68, 84 vs printed 186, 76, 57, 38, 67, 79.

table 2 (main p.9) intensity 12 mo hc vs pt prints nnt 63 (18-38). same root cause as c008: rr 1.05 (0.92-1.20) includes 1, so the interval is nnt benefit 18 to infinity to nnh 38 with the minus sign lost (rr-based approximation: nnt 16, nnh 39). under that reading 63 lies inside; as printed the point is outside its interval.

table 3 (main pp.10-11): 14 of 63 smd points lie outside their printed 95% cis (eg severity 12 mo pt vs uc -0.25 (-0.24 to 0.01)); 18 intervals are printed with descending limits (social, physical rows); in 20 cells the smd ci and md ci disagree on excluding zero (eg severity 12 mo pt vs uc md -0.4 (-0.6 to -0.2) but smd ci includes 0).

supp4 p.13 describes etable 8 as the primary analysis restricted to subsets, but etable 8 footnote b (p.14) lists only the base covariates (sex, age, site, residence, multisite pain, mental health, baseline severity), omitting the education and employment terms that etable 2 (p.7) adds to the primary models. the footnote is identical to etable 7's complete-case footnote. report contradicts itself on the subset model.

etable 2 (supp4 p.7) lists education among the additional nonresponse-weight predictors; the fitted weight model, etable 5 (p.10), has no education term but includes 'not employed'. workbook (supp5 etable 3) selection p values support employment (mcid p<.001, nonresponse p=.0228) and not education (no nonresponse p listed), so etable 2's list appears wrong.

etable 2 (supp4 p.7) specifies education as binary (any college vs hs or less), but etables 3 and 4 (pp.8-9) fit three nonreference education terms, two of them labeled 'aa degree' (eg etable 4 rr 0.97 and 1.16). the workbook (supp5) has four education levels (hs or less, associate's/technical, college, doctoral/postgraduate), consistent with a 4-level coding and a duplicated label.

etable 3 (supp4 p.8): 7 rows have 95% cis excluding 0 but p>.05 (eg pattern 2 -0.28 (-0.47 to -0.08), p=.150). printed p values reproduce almost exactly if each interval is estimate +/- 1 se (r = 0.999 over rows with p>=.001; se implied by p is 1.95 x the 95%-ci se), so the 'cis' are ~68% intervals. the three ratio rows in etables 4-5 (age, second aa, peg) are compatible with rounding.

etable 8 first header (supp4 p.14): 'n=454; 366 with at least 1 follow-up; pt=149, hc=153, uc=152 at 3-months'. 149+153+152 = 454 = n randomized, which exceeds the 366 with any follow-up, so these are not 3-month counts. by subtraction (etable 1 minus the post-8/9/2021 header) the 3-month counts would be uc 109, pt 94, hc 108 (total 311).

etable 11 (supp4 p.17) is titled and headed 'raw score median (25%-tile, 75%-tile)' but the text (p.15) calls the values means; bounds such as 5.1 (4.9, 5.2) for a 0-10 score (baseline sd 1.6) are far too narrow for iqrs and look like 95% cis of means. group columns also appear to be in the order uc, pt, hc, not the labeled pt, hc, uc: printed mds match differences under uc/pt/hc (mean abs error 0.03) but not as labeled (1.02).

supp5 workbook, sheet 'etable 3', e82: all observed (n=1568, 2 missing per e83) current depression '711 (73.2)'. 711/1566 = 45.4%. row reconciles otherwise: 162+243+711 = 1116 (b82), and b82 1116/2329 = 47.9%, c82 162/295 = 54.9%, d82 243/468 = 51.9% reproduce.

main p.3 describes promis-29 as 7 domains (raw 4-20 each) of mixed direction, yet p.6 and etable 4 (supp3 p.15) report one 'promis-29 score' (about 65, sd 14) and an adjusted md of -0.37 (-3.34 to 2.61) with no aggregation, transformation or favorable direction stated; protocol p.70 describes domain t-scores (mean 50, sd 10). also main p.6 levodopa mean 66 vs etable 4 64.74.

etable 3/4 footnote b (supp4 pp.6, 8) says crude ors with exact 95% cis; the printed cis match log-wald (woolf) intervals, not exact conditional ones. e.g., pda surgery 5/319 vs 3/308: or 1.62, wald 0.38-6.83 = printed; exact 0.31-10.51.

etable 1b (supp2 p.37): versions 11.100.131 and 122.100.407 each show 5 (5%) of the 183 ai participants; 5/183=2.7%. the other seven rows reproduce with n=183 (e.g., 58/183=31.7%->32; 109/183=59.6%->60).

main p.3 says the primary analysis was adjusted on the minimization stratification factors, which p.2 defines as etiology and center; table 2 footnote c (p.6) says the fine-gray model was adjusted for etiology only, as does the sap §3.5 (supp2 p.6, ocr). the two report descriptions of the same model differ by center.

methods (main p.3) describe mixed-effects logistic models but table 2 reports rrs with no conversion stated. the headline 'crude' rr 3.0 (2.0-4.9) differs from the crude ratio 300/720 vs 55/360 = 2.73 and from etable 8 'all' unadjusted rr 2.890 (1.983-4.709) for the same itt outcome.

main p.5 lists irritability 40.5% vs 43.4% and anxiety 33.3% vs 36.8% (any symptom, mhealth vs usual care) and then says irritability and anxiety were more common with mhealth. from etable 10 (supp2 p.15) any-symptom rates are lower with mhealth; only moderate/severe are higher (15.5% vs 8.4%; 9.3% vs 3.9%).

many rr intervals in table 2 and etables 8-9 are not symmetric on the log scale (python check), but with an unstated derivation (c006) asymmetry is not itself an error. demonstrable errors in these rows: adjusted self-report rr '2.8 (1.9 to 42)' (table 2 p.6; 4.2 intended) and mixed precision '3.6 (2.14 to 6.87)'.

etable 4 (supp2 p.6), usual care column: drug user 1 (7.4%) and severe pneumonia 1 (7.4%); 1/27 = 3.7%. also small rounding slips: 16/27 = 59.3% (printed 59.2), 8/52 = 15.4% (15.2), 3/52 = 5.8% (5.7).

etable 6 (supp2 p.9): control site 2008 deaths 5 (7.5%); with 40 recruited per cluster (etable 5 p.8), 5/40 = 12.5%. the count is right: control-site deaths sum to 27 and mhealth to 25, matching figure 1.

etable 9 (supp2 p.13) treatment failure 0.1% vs 0.6% with absolute difference +0.5 (-0.4 to 1.3); mhealth minus usual care is -0.5. same sign reversal in main table 2 (p.6) for death (3.5 vs 7.5; printed +4, 1.0 to 7.1) and treatment failure (0.1 vs 0.5; printed +0.4), whereas other rows are mhealth minus usual care.

etable 10 (supp2 p.22) day-15 immunoparalysis row: 40/106 vs 29/122, or printed 1.194 (1.09 to 3.45), i.e., point estimate below its ci. computed or = (40x93)/(66x29) = 1.94 (woolf 1.10-3.45); '1.194' is a typo for 1.94.

etable 13 (supp2 p.27): any serious teae in mals 20/25 (80.0%) with anakinra vs 21/23 (91.3%) with placebo, rd -11.3 points (fewer events on treatment). etable 15 (p.44) reports this as nnh1 = 8.8, i.e., harm; 1/0.113 = 8.8 is a number needed to benefit.

etable 15 (supp2 p.44) gives finite nnh1 intervals for mals (3.2 to 10.0) and immunoparalysis (9.9 to 55.8), but the underlying sae differences are nonsignificant (fisher p=.42 and .67), so the rd cis include 0 and the nnt/nnh intervals must pass through infinity.

efigure 7-9 panel a (supp2 pp.51-53, rendered): fisher p computed from printed counts reproduces most rows but not efig 7 apache>=25 (.439 vs .303), cci>=5 (.003 vs <.001), sofa>=10 (.035 vs .007), efig 9 sofa>=10 (.209 vs .147); efig 8 sofa>=10 .045 vs .034 (yates .044). no row changes significance.

efigure 7 and 8 panel b (supp2 pp.51-52): 'apache ii >=25' or 0.47 (0.30-1.62), p=.70. the ci is centered (log scale) at 0.697 and implies p about .08 for or 0.47; the printed p equals the ci midpoint, suggesting a transposed cell.

figure 3 (main p.9) columns labeled 'rate per 100 patient-years' contain 71.0/71.0 for all patients (and 30.5 + 40.5 = 71.0 for sex), whereas the primary rates are 2.30 and 2.44 per 100 patient-years (pp.1, 6, 8). the values are patient-years in hundreds, not rates.
etable 4 (supp3 p.33) chronotype 1388/818/520 vs 352/154/125 with p=0.09; chi-square from these counts gives p=0.018 (fisher 0.017). other rows reproduce (sex p=.11; smoking .004).
etable 5 (supp3 p.37) ethnicity: the 'other' row repeats the white row (40 (90.9) / 53 (93.0)), so ethnicity categories sum to 85 and 107 against n=44 and 57.

etable 5 (supp3 p.39): diuretic 9 (20.5) vs 16 (28.1), p=0.34 and combination bp med 9 (20.5) vs 16 (28.1), p=0.38: identical counts with different p values. 9/44 vs 16/57 gives uncorrected chi-square p=0.38, so the diuretic row's counts (or p) are wrong.
etable 8 (supp3 p.46, rendered) 'other reason/cannot remember', arb bedtime column: 1/37 printed as 7.7%; 1/37 = 2.7%. neighboring cells reproduce (2/38 = 5.3%; 2/26 = 7.7%).

table 1 (main p.5): midline shift median (iqr) with [n = 161] in each arm, footnote d 'data provided for unilateral csdh only', but unilateral csdh totals are 127 and 130 (thickness n = 122 each). 161 exceeds the unilateral population.
